fix: Stop cloning the stored route on every Move. Borrow it: `let route: &[ElementId] = self.input.raw_pointer_routes.get(&key).map_or(&[], Vec::as_slice);` for the Move arm (and the Up-with-buttons arm), and iterate `route` directly in the callback loop, calling `self.listener_callbacks(id)` and `self.localized_event(id, event)` per id (both take &self and return owned Rc clones), so no intermediate `callbacks` Vec is built either.

Avoid a HashSet and an unsized Vec per pointer event (called from dispatch_listeners on every event, from dispatch_pointer_signal and from dispatch_raw_trackpad_gesture). Hit lists are short: `let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(elements.len()); for &id in elements { if !out.contains(&id) && matches!(self.raw_input_kind(id), Some(RawInputKind::Listener { .. })) { out.push(id); } } out`. If the caller can take a reused scratch buffer, return into it instead of allocating.

Every non-Enter/Exit pointer event allocates `next` here, plus `next.clone()` at line 622 for the map. Keep the per-device hover set in a reusable buffer: swap a scratch Vec in (`let mut next = std::mem::take(&mut self.input.hover_scratch); next.clear(); next.extend(...)`), then `std::mem::swap` it with the stored entry in `self.input.mouse_hover` so the previous buffer becomes the next scratch. Removes both the collect and the clone in steady state.

dispatch_mouse_regions collects previous_live, exits, enters, exit_callbacks, enter_callbacks, enter_behaviors, exit_behaviors and hover_callbacks, each a Vec, on every mouse move. Walk the borrowed slices instead: exit pass `for id in previous.iter().copied().filter(|id| self.elements.contains(id.0) && !next.contains(id))`, enter pass `for id in next.iter().copied().filter(|id| !previous_live.contains(id))` with the same ordering (exits, then exit behaviors, then enters in reverse, then enter behaviors), and resolve `mouse_region_config` / `focus_behavior_for` inline at call time. Callbacks are owned Rc clones so no self borrow is held across the call.

Called from dispatch_mouse_regions on every mouse event and allocates whenever a focus-behavior detector encloses the pointer. Pass a `&mut Vec<ElementId>` scratch buffer from the caller (or push directly into the enter/exit scratch) instead of returning a fresh Vec.

Every primary Down/Up walks the whole element arena once per tap surface, and calls nearest_tap_surface (an ancestor walk) for each element, so the cost is O(elements x depth) per pointer event. Maintain the per-surface tap-region list incrementally (set on mount/update of TapRegion/TextFieldTapRegion, remove on unmount, the same way raw_input_unmounted already cleans routes), or at least walk only the surface's subtree. Also avoids cloning callbacks and group ids into a fresh Vec each press.

Per surface, per Down/Up, this builds `surfaces` (line 757), `hit_groups` HashSet (773), `inside` Vec (778), `inside_ids` HashSet (788) and `outside` Vec (792). Use a single pass over `registrations` with a per-registration `inside: bool` computed from `hit` and a small group list (`Vec` with `contains`, groups are few), and iterate the two callback sets directly. Reuse one scratch buffer for the surface list if it still allocates.

raw_gesture_factories (line 826) clones the whole factory slice (`map_or_else(Vec::new, ToOwned::to_owned)`) for every element in the hit list on each primary Down. The clone exists only to dodge the &mut self.input borrow. Use split borrows instead: take `let factories = self.elements.get(element.0).and_then(|e| match e.widget.kind() { WidgetKind::RawInput { kind, .. } => kind.factory_map(), _ => None }).unwrap_or(&[]);` and mutate `self.input.raw_recognizers` through the field directly (disjoint from `self.elements`), so no Vec<ErasedGestureRecognizerFactory> is cloned.

Runs on every primary Down that starts a raw gesture stream and allocates a HashSet plus a result Vec. Hit lists are short: replace the HashSet with `out.contains(&id)` over the output Vec (`Vec::with_capacity(hit.len())`), and only keep elements whose `factory_map()` is non-empty, which is already the filter predicate.

Every non-Down event on an active raw gesture stream (every Move/Up/Cancel) allocates `active_members` here, and `self.input.gesture_arena.entries(key)` (line 908, also re-called at 950 and 955) allocates a Vec on each call. Iterate the members by index with Copy tuples (`for i in 0..len { let (element, member, type_id) = { let m = &self.input.raw_gesture_streams[&key].members[i]; (m.element, m.member, m.type_id) }; ... }`) and add a non-allocating `GestureArena::disposition(key, member) -> Option<GestureDisposition>` in incular-gestures/src/arena.rs to replace the `entries` snapshot lookups via `disposition_for`.

`.map(ToOwned::to_owned)` clones the full factory slice on every raw-input sync, only to release the borrow of self before mutating self.input.raw_recognizers. Replace with the split-borrow form (read factories from self.elements via a field-level match, then mutate self.input.raw_recognizers), or collect only the `type_id()` values if the factories themselves are not needed after the recognizer loop.

The Vec is collected only to be iterated once. Drop the binding and loop over the chain directly: `for callback in self.listener_ids(&self.raw_hit_elements(position)).into_iter().filter_map(|id| self.listener_callbacks(id)).filter_map(|cb| cb.on_trackpad_gesture) { callback(event); }`. The chain borrows only &self, so this is sound.

`cursor_at` is a pure alias of `mouse_cursor_at` with no callers in the workspace. Per the pre-1.0 policy (no aliases or dead code kept around), delete it and record a CHANGELOG `**Breaking (incular-widgets):**` note with the migration to `mouse_cursor_at`.
